newsitem.title: GERMANY: Vranitzky says Albania conflict could spread - radio.
newsitem.headline: Vranitzky says Albania conflict could spread - radio.

text.p: Former Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky said on Thursday the conflict in Albania could spread through the Balkans and denied that President Sali Berisha was opposed to an OSCE delegation visiting his country.

Vranitzky, special envoy to Albania for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), said in an interview with Deutsche Welle radio that an OSCE delegation made up of diplomats from Poland, Denmark and Switzerland had left for Albania on Thursday.
"There is a danger that the conflict in Albania could expand to other areas in the Balkans," Vranitzky said, according to a text of the interview released in Bonn.
"The Albania mission from the OSCE will take place as planned," he said. "An advance delegation of diplomats from Poland, Denmark and Switzerland left for Albania today."

Vranitzky added that he had assured Berisha in a telephone conversation on Thursday that the OSCE delegation would not "prosecute him like an enemy." He said that Berisha was important for a peaceful resolution to the conflict.

More than 20 people have been reported killed in Albania's south in violent protests sparked by the collapse of several get-rich-quick investment schemes. A night-time curfew has been ordered and troops have been called in to quell the unrest.
